source_issues.finding: The full-decomposition convention defines rectangular Sigma; Sigma^2 in the PCA block is dimensionally undefined unless silently switching to a square reduced Sigma. Exercise U = A V Sigma^{-1} likewise is not a general full-SVD recipe for rectangular/rank-deficient matrices. All formula text preserved.
Orthogonal factors may include reflection, not only rotation. For zero singular values, the mapped vector is zero with no direction. The source omits these qualifications; no silent correction.
Source says any matrix but uses transpose/orthogonal forms suited to real matrices. Complex-matrix SVD uses conjugate transpose and unitary factors. No scope added to translation.

Noise/signal separation assumptions are overbroad; normal-equation inverse requires full column rank; condition number describes sensitivity of solving/inversion rather than unconditional forward output changes; generic power iteration targets largest-modulus eigenvalue and needs spectral/start conditions. Source wording preserved.

Lesson code block power iteration divides by norm without zero guard; linked svd.py guards small norm. Pseudoinverse example divides all singular values, while linked function thresholds zeros. Example is full rank, but not a generic singular-matrix implementation.
Blanket sklearn PCA uses SVD, not eigendecomposition is version/solver dependent. Frozen source claim retained; no current-library verification performed.

Full SVD defines Sigma as m x n. Sigma^2 in the PCA block and Sigma^{-1} in the full-SVD exercise are not general rectangular-matrix operations. A reduced square Sigma and nonzero-value/rank restrictions would be needed. The source formula bytes are preserved.
Orthogonal factors may reflect as well as rotate; zero singular values map vectors to zero, which has no output direction. Source simplifications are retained.
The any-matrix claim is broader than the real-matrix transpose/orthogonal convention shown; complex SVD needs conjugate transpose and unitary factors. Source scope is unchanged.

The source omits assumptions behind low-rank signal/noise separation, full-column-rank normal-equation inversion, condition-number sensitivity statements, and convergence to the largest-modulus eigenvalue for power iteration. These are source qualifications, not translation corrections.

The embedded power iteration has no zero-norm guard, and the embedded pseudoinverse divides every singular value without thresholding. Linked Python routines guard small values; the displayed least-squares example itself is full rank.

The referenced Julia script imports LinearAlgebra and Random but uses mean without importing Statistics. A normal standalone Julia run reaches mean in demo_image_compression; this is a source-code runtime defect, not a translation defect. Not executed.
